questions.explanation: An impairment loss on an asset not previously revalued is recognised in profit or loss, not OCI.

questions.question: A Co has publicly traded shares and reports profit after tax of $100 million for the year ended 31 December 20X0. On 1 January 20X0, the entity had 200 million ordinary shares in issue and $80 million 6% irredeemable preference shares. The preference dividends are payable on 31 December each year. In accordance with IAS 33 Earnings per share (EPS), What is the EPS for the year ended 31 December 20X0?

options.A: 34.0 cents
options.B: 35.7 cents
options.C: 47.6 cents
options.D: 50.0 cents

questions.explanation: Preference dividend = $80m * 6% = $4.8m; EPS = ($100m - $4.8m) / 200m shares = $0.476 = 47.6 cents.

questions.question: IAS 19 provides guidance on accounting for employee benefits, including defined benefit pensions, which statements are correct? 1. The current services cost in a year is recognized in other comprehensive income. 2. Remeasurements include the difference between the actual and expected return on plan assets. 3. Recognition of a pension surplus is restricted by the asset ceiling. 4. Past service costs are spread over an employee's remaining expected working life.

options.A: 1 and 2
options.B: 1 and 3
options.C: 2 and 3
options.D: 1 and 4

questions.explanation: Remeasurements include return differences/actuarial gains or losses (2), and net defined benefit assets are subject to the asset ceiling (3).

questions.question: According to IAS 12 Income Taxes, where the tax base of an asset exceeds its carrying amount in the statement of financial position, what term describes the difference?

options.A: A taxable temporary difference
options.B: A deferred tax asset
options.C: A deductible temporary difference
options.D: A deferred tax liability

questions.explanation: When an asset's tax base exceeds its carrying amount, future tax deductions will exceed accounting deductions, creating a deductible temporary difference.

questions.question: Y Co used some but not all IFRSs in its financial statements to 31 December 20X4.In the year to 31 December 20X5, Y Co is to adopt all IFRSs. Which of the following statements is true under IFRS1, First time Adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards?

options.A: In the year to 31 December 20X4, Y is considered to be a first time adopter
options.B: In the year to 31 December 20X5, Y is not considered to be a first time adopter
options.C: In the year to 31 December 20X5, Y is considered to be a first time adopter
options.D: Y is not a first time adopter in 20X4 or 20X5

questions.explanation: Applying only some IFRSs is not full IFRS compliance; when Y Co adopts all IFRSs in 20X5 with an explicit and unreserved statement of compliance, it is a first-time adopter.

questions.question: IAS 23 Borrowing Costs outlines the treatment of borrowing costs and whether they should be added to the capitalized cost of an asset. Which of the following statements are correct? 1. Interest on a financial lease liability may be an eligible borrowing cost 2. Capitalization of interest is suspended if construction of an asset is suspended for an extended period 3. Interest on general borrowings can never be capitalized.

options.A: 1 and 2
options.B: 1 and 3
options.C: 2 and 3
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

questions.explanation: Finance lease interest can be an eligible borrowing cost (1), capitalisation is suspended during extended periods of active development suspension (2), and general borrowings can be capitalised using a capitalisation rate.

questions.question: Under IAS 19 Employee Benefits, which of the following statements is true in relation to accounting for pension schemes? In the year to 31 December 20X4, Y is considered to be a first time adopter

options.A: Remeasurements of a defined benefit scheme should be recognized immediately in profit or loss
options.B: Remeasurements of a defined benefit scheme should be deferred and spread over the average reaming working life of employees using the corridor approach
options.C: Employer contributions to a defined contribution scheme are recognized as an expense in profit or loss
options.D: Employer contributions to a defined contribution scheme increase the fair value of the pension asset in the statement of financial position.

questions.explanation: Contributions payable to a defined contribution plan are recognised as an expense in profit or loss.

questions.question: Which body of the IFRS Foundation provides a link between the Foundation and public authorities and also approves the appointment of IFRS Foundation Trustees?

options.A: The IFRS Interpretations Committee
options.B: The Monitoring Board
options.C: The International Accounting Standards Board
options.D: The IFRS Advisory Council

questions.explanation: The Monitoring Board provides a link with public capital market authorities and approves Trustee appointments.

questions.question: IAS 27 Separate Financial Statements states that in the separate financial statements (i.e. not the consolidated financial statements) of an investor, an investment in an associate should be:

options.A: Held at cost or in accordance with IFRS 9 or equity method
options.B: Valued using the equity method of accounting
options.C: Held at fair value only
options.D: Held at cost

questions.explanation: In separate financial statements, investments in subsidiaries, joint ventures, and associates are accounted for at cost, in accordance with IFRS 9, or using the equity method.

questions.question: IAS 21 'The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates' requires that any exchange difference on translation of a foreign operation's financial statements should be accumulated in a separate component of equity. On disposal of such a foreign operation, the cumulative amount of exchange differences held in that operation should be:

options.A: Reclassified to profit or loss as part of the gain or loss on disposal
options.B: Left in a separate component of equity
options.C: Transferred to retained earnings
options.D: Recognized as an extraordinary item in the statement of profit or loss

questions.explanation: Cumulative translation differences are reclassified from equity to profit or loss when the foreign operation is disposed of.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements regarding IFRS 16 leases is true?

options.A: A lessor recognizes a receivable in respect of a lease for an asset that is so specialized that only the lessee could use it without major modification
options.B: Lessees apply the same accounting treatment to all leases
options.C: A lessor deducts initial direct costs incurred in arranging an operating lease from the carrying amount of leased asset
options.D: In a sale and leaseback transaction if a transfer is a sale, proceeds are recognized as a financial liability

questions.explanation: A lease of a specialised asset usable only by the lessee without major modification indicates a finance lease, where the lessor recognises a lease receivable.

questions.question: Which statement is correct regarding the 2018 Conceptual Framework?

options.A: Current value measurements include fair value and value in use
options.B: An asset is recognized if its probable that economics benefits will flow to an entity
options.C: Part of an entity cannot be a reporting entity
options.D: All income and expenses must be measured in profit or loss without exception

questions.explanation: Current value measurement bases under the Conceptual Framework include fair value, value in use (for assets) / fulfilment value (for liabilities), and current cost.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct when accounting for business combinations?

options.A: Goodwill must be tested for impairment only when indicators exist
options.B: Provisions for future restructuring costs arising from the business combination should be recognized in applying the acquisition method
options.C: Goodwill must be tested at least annually for impairment
options.D: An impairment loss arising on full goodwill is allocated between the group and NCI in proportion to the carrying amount of their respective goodwill balances

questions.explanation: Per the answer key in the source file, option D is selected.

questions.question: In accordance with IFRS 11 Joint Arrangements, a joint venture should be incorporated into the group financial statements using:

options.A: Full line-by-line consolidation
options.B: Proportionate consolidation only
options.C: Equity accounting only
options.D: Proportionate consolidation or equity accounting

questions.explanation: Under IFRS 11, an interest in a joint venture is accounted for using the equity method.

questions.question: On 31 December 20X8 one of Pattinson Co's properties met the criteria to be classified as held for sale. The property was measured under the revaluation model; its fair value at 31 December 20X7 was $25million and after depreciation for the year, its carrying amount at 31 December 20X8 was $24.5 million. At 31 December 20X8 the property had a fair value of $27 million. Selling costs are 4% of fair value. What net amount is recognized in Pattinson Co's profit or loss in the year ended 31 December 20X8 in respect of the property?

options.A: $500,000 expense
options.B: $1,080,000 expense
options.C: $1,580,000 expense

questions.explanation: FV less costs to sell = $27m * 96% = $25.92m > carrying amount $24.5m; depreciation for 20X8 = $25m - $24.5m = $0.5m ($500,000 expense).

questions.question: On 1 January 20X9, a company bought an item of plant costing $100,000. It received a government grant of $30,000 towards the purchase. The plant has a 5-year useful life. Which of the following to be reported in the financial statements for the year ended 31 December 20X9 reflects the requirements of IAS 20?

options.A: A depreciation charge of $14,000 and deferred income with a carrying amount of $24,000.
options.B: Grant income of nil and plant with a carrying amount of $56,000.
options.C: A depreciation charge of $20,000 and deferred income with a carrying amount of $30,000.
options.D: Grant income of $6,000 and plant with a carrying amount of $56,000

questions.explanation: Deducting the $30,000 grant from cost gives $70,000; depreciation = $70,000 / 5 = $14,000; carrying amount at 31 Dec 20X9 = $70,000 - $14,000 = $56,000 (grant income = nil).
